title: Ere God Had Built the Mountains
description: Ere God Had Built the Mountains in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 52, “Wisdom. Pr 8:22-31”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ere God had built the moun-tains, Or raised the fruit-ful hills; Be-fore he filled the foun-tains That feed the run-ning rills; In me, from ev-er-last-ing, The won-der-ful I Am, Found plea-sures nev-er wast-ing, And Wis-dom is my name.

lines: Ere God had built the mountains,
When, like a tent to dwell in,
He wrought by weight and measure,
And I was with him then;
And mine, the sons of men.
In wisdom thou hast made us,
And died for us in love.
Who when we saw thee, slighted
And nailed thee to a tree?
The voice that speaks in thunder,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
